Reduction in the Midri system.

Every result in this system is reduced modulo 100. That is, after computing a value you divide it by 100 and keep only the remainder. A result is therefore always between 0 and 99 inclusive.

Evaluation order in the Midri system.

When an expression contains more than one ^, the operator associates left to right. Parentheses, where written, are evaluated first.

A worked example.

Consider 7 ^ 4. Applying the rule gives 48.

The Midri System.

The Midri system introduces a single operator written ^. It combines two whole numbers and produces a whole number.

To evaluate x ^ y, square x, then add 1 times y, then subtract 5.

The Bravor System.

The Bravor system introduces a single operator written ~. It combines two whole numbers and produces a whole number.

To evaluate x ~ y, subtract y from x, multiply the difference by 4, then add 2.

A worked example.

Consider 7 ~ 4. Applying the rule gives 14.

Evaluation order in the Bravor system.

When an expression contains more than one ~, the operator associates right to left. Parentheses, where written, are evaluated first.

Reduction in the Bravor system.

Every result in this system is reduced modulo 1000. That is, after computing a value you divide it by 1000 and keep only the remainder. A result is therefore always between 0 and 999 inclusive.

The Cloxil System.

The Cloxil system introduces a single operator written ~. It combines two whole numbers and produces a whole number.

To evaluate x ~ y, multiply x by 4, multiply y by 3, add the two products, then add 5.

Reduction in the Cloxil system.

Every result in this system is reduced modulo 100. That is, after computing a value you divide it by 100 and keep only the remainder. A result is therefore always between 0 and 99 inclusive.
